seoTitle: Solar Beam: NASA Space Photos on All Apple Devices
metaDescription: See NASA's daily picture, James Webb images, and near-Earth asteroids in 4K on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV, and Vision Pro. One purchase unlocks them all.
keywords: astronomy picture of the day app
heroHeadline: The universe, on every screen you own
heroSubhead: Solar Beam shows NASA's picture of the day, the sharpest James Webb images ever taken, and the asteroids passing Earth right now — in 4K, no telescope required. One purchase covers iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV, and Vision Pro.
highlights: One US$19.99 purchase unlocks all five Apple platforms, with Family Sharing
A fresh NASA image every day, plus years of archives and the full Webb library
Live near-Earth asteroid readouts that update as NASA finds new objects

features.title: Picture of the Day
features.body: NASA picks one image of the cosmos every day. Solar Beam puts it on the big screen with plain-language facts so you understand what you're looking at.

features.title: The Webb Library
features.body: Browse the deepest images humanity has captured — newborn stars, colliding galaxies, and distant nebulae — in 4K with NASA's official descriptions.

features.title: Asteroid Tracker
features.body: See what's passing Earth in real time: how close each asteroid comes, how fast it moves, and the size of impact it would leave. Charts sort the dangerous from the safe.

features.title: Ambient Mode
features.body: Leave a deep-space gallery running on your TV, Mac, or in your room on Vision Pro. Cosmic wallpaper that changes itself.

features.title: Built for Each Platform
features.body: UIKit on iPhone and iPad, SwiftUI on Mac and Apple TV, RealityKit on Vision Pro. Each version is built for its device, not ported.

features.title: Works Offline
features.body: Smart caching means fast launches, and images you've already viewed stay available without a connection.

howItWorks.body: A single US$19.99 purchase unlocks Solar Beam on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV, and Vision Pro, shareable with your family.
Today's NASA picture greets you instantly, with the Webb library and live asteroid tracker one tap away.
Switch on Ambient Mode and let the cosmos play across your biggest screen, or read the facts behind each image.

faq.q: How much does Solar Beam cost?
faq.a: It's a one-time US$19.99 purchase on the App Store. There's no subscription. That single purchase covers iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV, and Vision Pro.

faq.q: Do I have to buy it again for each device?
faq.a: No. Solar Beam is a universal purchase — buy it once and it unlocks on all your Apple devices, shareable through Family Sharing.

faq.q: Is there a subscription or in-app purchase?
faq.a: No. The US$19.99 purchase unlocks everything, including Ambient Mode, the full Webb library, and the complete archive of daily pictures. No recurring fees.

faq.q: Where do the images and data come from?
faq.a: From NASA's public APIs: the Astronomy Picture of the Day, James Webb Space Telescope imagery, and near-Earth object data. Solar Beam is an independent app and is not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA or ESA.
Yes, for content you've already viewed. Smart caching keeps recent images available offline and makes launches fast. New daily images and live asteroid updates need a connection.
iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV, and Apple Vision Pro. It requires iOS, iPadOS, macOS, or tvOS 18 or later (visionOS for Vision Pro).
Refunds are handled by Apple through your App Store account, under Apple's standard refund policy. Solar Beam doesn't process payments directly.
Short, plain-language explanations paired with each image to help the science click — from solar flares to galaxies billions of light-years away.
